atomic_source_supported_statements.statement: The paper treats SAXS and smFRET as distinct measurement families: RG is estimated from SAXS, while RE for fluorescently labeled termini is estimated from smFRET.

The SAXS object shown by the paper is a scattering-intensity profile I(q) as a function of momentum transfer q. RG is then calculated from that profile by a stated analysis, rather than being the raw observation itself.

The smFRET object shown by the paper is EFRET, including burst-wise measurements and a mean EFRET. The reported RE,L is inferred using a distribution P(rD,A; RE,L) and a dye-pair-specific Forster distance R0.

The paper says the functional form of the interdye-distance distribution is unknown a priori and may be chosen from polymer models such as a Gaussian chain, self-avoiding random walk, or a sphere model.

SAXS intensities are weighted averages over molecules and conformations in solution and provide global chain-dimension information, whereas smFRET probes the donor-acceptor separation at the labeled termini and can follow motions from nanosecond to millisecond regimes.
The article reports different protein-concentration regimes for the two experiments and explicitly says it tested whether that difference explained the discrepancy in their inferences.

The discussion distinguishes integral averaging of distance distributions in SAXS from differential averaging of one end-to-end distance in smFRET and reports that ensembles matching SAXS can remain incompatible with smFRET-derived inferences, especially away from denaturing conditions.

native_observable_by_source.value: Scattering intensity profile I(q) as a function of momentum transfer q, measured for labeled and unlabeled samples.

estimand_by_source.value: The paper reports RG,U and RG,L as estimates of global size; it also uses full scattering profiles for size-distribution and shape information.

spatial_support_by_source.value: Global molecular/chain dimensions, based on interatomic distances within molecules and averaged over the conformations of molecules in solution.

time_or_ensemble_averaging_by_source.value: The paper describes scattering intensities as weighted averages over all protein molecules and conformations in solution. It does not present a time-resolved kinetic SAXS estimate in the main-text passages used here.

inverse_or_forward_model_assumptions.value: RG is calculated from I(q) versus q through the Guinier approximation or a pair-distance distribution function.
Finite-concentration interpretation assumes the absence of intermolecular interactions in the cited introductory framing.

statistical_unit_by_source.value: A SAXS profile for a specified protein, labeling state, and buffer condition; the study describes labeled and unlabeled samples at micromolar-and-beyond concentrations.

uncertainty_or_ambiguity_boundaries.value: SAXS averaging makes it difficult to assess populations and fluctuations smaller than global dimensions.
Detailed experimental settings and supporting analyses are cited to the Supporting Information, which is outside this main-article-only record.

native_observable_by_source.value: Single-molecule FRET efficiencies EFRET, including a burst-wise distribution and mean EFRET from doubly labeled proteins.

estimand_by_source.value: The paper uses mean EFRET to infer RE,L, the ensemble-averaged root-mean-squared distance between donor and acceptor dyes. RE,L is presented as a proxy for the actual end-to-end distance RE,U, not as the same quantity.

spatial_support_by_source.value: The source object's direct geometric support is the donor-acceptor separation at the specifically labeled terminal positions, rather than an all-pairs/global structural average.

time_or_ensemble_averaging_by_source.value: The paper identifies smFRET as able to follow motions from nanosecond to millisecond regimes; its source-to-distance mapping uses mean EFRET and a distance distribution. The inspected passages do not define a single kinetic-rate estimand.

inverse_or_forward_model_assumptions.value: RE,L is inferred from mean EFRET through P(rD,A; RE,L) and a dye-pair-specific R0.
The form of P(rD,A; RE,L) is unknown a priori and selected from polymer-model alternatives; flexible dye linkers make RE,L distinct from RE,U.

statistical_unit_by_source.value: Burst-wise EFRET measurements from a specified doubly labeled protein and condition, summarized as a mean EFRET at picomolar labeled-protein concentration.

uncertainty_or_ambiguity_boundaries.value: Dye placement, flexible linkers, dye-pair R0, and the distribution-model choice all affect the mapping from EFRET to RE,L.
The main article refers detailed FRET parameters, anisotropies, gamma/quantum-yield checks, and full efficiency datasets to the Supporting Information, which is not used here.

case_specific_assumptions.value: The paper's direct comparisons concern a defined set of proteins and labeled/unlabeled constructs under denaturing and near-native conditions; their results are not a universal modality conversion law.
This calibration uses only main-text passages, so it does not adjudicate SI-dependent numerical parameters or reproduce the paper's analyses.

maximum_source_supported_wording: For the Fuertes et al. source objects, SAXS records global scattering profiles from which RG and additional profile-derived size or shape information are estimated, while smFRET records EFRET from labeled termini and maps mean efficiency to an inferred dye-to-dye distance through stated distribution and dye assumptions. The paper supports keeping those measurement semantics distinct before any cross-source interpretation.
